premises.text: GDPR and related regulation ended the era of unrestricted corporate data sharing
premises.evidence_span: when GDPR came into effect last year, that era ended forever

premises.text: Companies share data with far more vendors than they realize and lack easy ways to track flows or meet privacy obligations
premises.evidence_span: there is no easy way to track what's happening with all of that data, and there's no easy way for companies to comply with their privacy obligations

premises.text: A privacy platform scores vendors from a proprietary dataset and surfaces lawsuits, policies, and risk for compliance decisions
premises.evidence_span: Utilizing our proprietary data set of 7,000 different vendors, Osano provides a 360-degree view of each vendor's privacy practices

premises.text: A managed cookie-consent solution with one line of code makes websites compliant across many countries' laws
premises.evidence_span: fully managed cookie consent solution, so that with one line of code, websites can immediately become compliant with the laws of 40 different countries

premises.text: A developer API lets builders embed data privacy into applications and workflows
premises.evidence_span: developer API so that developers can quickly build data privacy into their applications and their workflows

premises.text: The offering targets the majority of companies underserved by expensive, hard-to-use point solutions
premises.evidence_span: targeting the 90 percent of companies who are not served by the expensive point solutions

value.text: Companies can easily identify vendor privacy risk and comply with privacy laws
value.evidence_span: makes it easy for companies to identify which vendors are best to work with, to comply with laws like GDPR

causal_links.evidence_span: Osano makes it easy, one place to see your SaaS vendors, their privacy risks and their ratings
not served by the expensive point solutions

notes: Lawsuit browsing, policy tracking, and consent dialog language folded into vendor/consent platform premises (§4.1(5)); cookie consent kept distinct from vendor scoring because it is framed as a separate website-compliance mechanism. Singleton D3: go-to-market wedge vs OneTrust is independently revisable. Free-user counts and consent volume excluded as traction; team bios and discount CTA excluded. Market-spend forecast treated as framing, not a premise.
